The Expected Information in nu of a Multivariate t

Source: R/mvstudent_t_distrib.R
mvt_info_nunu.Rd

Computes $$I_{\nu\nu} = \tfrac{1}{4}\left\{\psi'\!\left(\tfrac{\nu}{2}\right) - \psi'\!\left(\tfrac{\nu+p}{2}\right)\right\} - \frac{p(\nu+p+4)}{2\nu(\nu+p)(\nu+p+2)}$$ without the cancellation of the direct form, whose terms are of order \(\nu^{-2}\) while the result is of order \(\nu^{-4}\).

Usage

mvt_info_nunu(nu, p)

Arguments

nu

The degrees of freedom, a numeric vector of positive values.

p

The dimension, a single positive whole number.

Value

A numeric vector as long as nu, the information, which is positive; the expected second derivative is its negative.

Details

Both parts are Laplace transforms: \(I_{\nu\nu} = \int_0^\infty e^{-\nu t}\phi(t)\,dt\) with $$\phi(t) = t\,g(t) - \alpha + e^{-pt} - \gamma\,e^{-(p+2)t}, \qquad \alpha = \frac{p+4}{2(p+2)}, \quad \gamma = \frac{p}{2(p+2)},$$ \(g\) as in mvt_nu_coef(). The first three derivatives of \(\phi\) at zero vanish, so \(I_{\nu\nu} = \sum_{k \ge 3} \phi^{(k)}(0)/\nu^{k+1}\); this series is summed for \(\nu \ge \max(20, 4(p+2))\) and the direct form is used below.

See also

distrib_expected_hessian.MvStudentTDistrib(), the consumer, and mvt_nu_coef() for the series.

Examples

nu <- c(10, 1e4, 1e8)
direct <- (trigamma(nu / 2) - trigamma((nu + 3) / 2)) / 4 -
  3 * (nu + 7) / (2 * nu * (nu + 3) * (nu + 5))
rbind(exact = distributions7:::mvt_info_nunu(nu, 3), direct = direct)
#>                [,1]         [,2]          [,3]
#> exact  0.0006826819 1.348891e-15  1.350000e-31
#> direct 0.0006826819 1.348811e-15 -2.588087e-24
